evidence:
Inspected the actual frozen XLSX using openpyxl: Quality Checks row 24 (number 23), cells A24:D24, and Internal Quality Checks row 24, cells A24:D24/E24/H24. The public row requires every test.sh launch assumption to be disclosed and explicitly says the network is public; the older internal same-origin wording does not override that. Applied frozen SKILL.md, quality-checks.md section 23, staged-task-contract.md sections tests/test.sh and Cross-file agreements, deterministic-checks.md check-runtime-contract-strings.py/check-verifier-contract.py, and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md.

The ordinary launch contract agrees: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/instruction.md:5,9 directs the builder to all six /instructions notes and requires the finished app and built frontend in /app. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/environment/instructions/integration.md:3,5,7,9,11,13 names Node 22, Express, better-sqlite3, NODE_PATH, node /app/server.js, 0.0.0.0:3000, /app/public/index.html, successful prompt GET /api/health, DB_PATH with /app/app.db fallback, self-contained runtime assets, no startup installs, and the exact allowed node_modules symlink boundary. These match .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/test.sh:68-111,136-167. Both Dockerfiles provide express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1. All five prompt openings and app_context.md:4 use localhost:3000. The /api/health success requirement is checked independently in gates/constraints/judge.toml:23; the liveness probe accepting an HTTPError is therefore not by itself a demonstrated health false-pass. The sanitized PATH/HOME and redundant PORT=3000 do not by themselves require an extra application feature; a compliant app can use fixed port 3000 and absolute /app paths. No imposed React/Vite choice or app-wide same-origin requirement was found.

Confirmed inherited restart mismatch: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/environment/instructions/integration.md:7 promises survival of a "complete process restart over the same database"; it does not require the process to terminate on SIGTERM within five seconds. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/test.sh:152-159 sends only SIGTERM and waits 50 times 0.1 seconds, then proceeds even if the old process group is still alive. Lines 160-183 spawn a replacement, replace app.pid, and return success based solely on an HTTP response, without checking that the old group is gone or the new PID remains alive. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:45-47 turns that zero exit into "restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP". The functional consumer at .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:409-415 then treats that completion as the single actual restart for the durability/write observations. This creates an undocumented shutdown assumption and can substitute the old process for the public complete-restart contract.

Independently verified the supplied raw reproduction, not a reviewer summary: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-repair3/inherited-restart-counterexample.json has SHA256 552bf6e7afa7707d093667e2e2d35fe8bbd88b54deedd73a401d22586fcc2e98, matching raw-evidence-index.json. Its executed driver qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-09-30/reproduce_restart.py has SHA256 ef6d94b64ff5635e0e1fb69e5eaefea9e0d83cbe2004714c2510e7aa163c164a and extracts the helper verbatim from test.sh before placeholder substitution. Recomputed current test.sh SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa and helper SHA256 0db23e8c7c8d70c7e934c4d13ccbb2326a4da2cb47f1b2ba1967009d829be3b7; both equal the recorded reproduction inputs. Observations: helper_returncode=0, old_pid=7, claimed_new_pid=67, old_still_running=true, before.pid=7, after.pid=7, and replacement log EADDRINUSE followed by "app-restart pid=67 ready=1". Thus the runtime false success is directly observed for these helper bytes.

The current test.sh and tests/Dockerfile are byte-identical to their frozen template counterparts; this is a genuine inherited harness conflict, not task-specific drift and not permission to edit canonical files. The raw golden actual-restart.json and launch_workflow.py show a cooperative golden process did exit and change PID 16 to 338, so the failure is conditional; that successful case does not refute the resistant-process witness. No new execution, provider call, or Docker run was performed. Full configured judge, Oracle and target-model results remain unmeasured; neither raw scripted timing nor this source/reproduction audit establishes those results.
counterexample: Executed raw witness: a Node HTTP server with process.on("SIGTERM",()=>{}) remains the port-3000 responder after restart_app helper completion; the exact frozen helper reports success although its new process dies with EADDRINUSE. A SQLite-backed app with delayed/ignored graceful shutdown is not forbidden by the public launch contract, and a complete externally enforced restart remains meaningful for it. Broken extension (reasoned, not executed as a full app): an otherwise usable saved library held only in process memory can keep returning the recorded fields from the surviving old process and receive apparent S22 restart durability/write credit, despite losing all records after a real termination/relaunch. Considered a relative-path/cwd false-fail as well, but did not count it: the public note explicitly supplies absolute /app paths, and no specific working directory is promised.
suggested_fix: Escalate the inherited helper issue to the canonical harness owner: enforce bounded old-group termination, verify replacement PID liveness and successful replacement, and report failed replacement as unavailable evidence; preserve frozen harness files in this review and remeasure the resistant-process witness after an authorized canonical update.
